short.title: Talking-head tip
short.bestFor: One useful point, said straight to camera, with one example you can show.
short.footage: One take of you making the point, plus a shot or screen recording of the example.
short.example: Worked example: why your captions get covered.
short.rhythm: Something changes on screen every 2–3 seconds: a cut, a punch-in, a caption pop or a cutaway.
checks: Mute it. Can you follow the tip from the on-screen text and captions alone?
Scrub through. Is there any stretch of 3 seconds where nothing changes?
Play the last line straight into the first. Does the loop make sense?

beats.title: Hook
beats.goal: Name the mistake in one breath, with the stakes on screen from the first frame.
beats.show: Your face, a stakes line in the upper third, captions on.
beats.line: If your captions sit at the bottom of the screen, half your viewers can't read them.

beats.title: Why it happens
beats.goal: Say why it happens in one sentence. No intro, no 'so today'.
beats.show: The problem itself: the app's buttons sitting over the captions.
beats.line: The app puts its own buttons and caption right on top of that space.

beats.title: The fix
beats.goal: Give the fix as one instruction they can copy today.
beats.show: Back on your face, punching in on the key word.
beats.line: Move them up to just below the middle of the frame, and keep each line to three words.

beats.title: Show it working
beats.goal: Prove it with a before and after on the same clip.
beats.show: Split screen: captions at the bottom on top, moved up underneath.
beats.line: Same clip, same captions. Only the position changed, and nothing covers them now.

beats.title: Re-hook
beats.goal: Open one more question so they stay for the last part.
beats.show: A quick zoom, a new line of text and one sound.
beats.line: But there's one more spot people forget to check.

beats.title: The extra tip
beats.goal: Pay off the re-hook straight away.
beats.show: Zoom into the exact spot on the screen.
beats.line: The top of the screen. Your username and the audio label sit there, so keep text below them.

beats.title: Verdict
beats.goal: Say the whole tip again in one short line.
beats.show: A full-screen slam on the key words.
beats.line: Middle of the frame, three words a line. That's it.

beats.title: End
beats.goal: End on a line that sends them back to the start, or a soft ask to save it. No end card.
beats.show: Your face. Hold one beat, then cut.
beats.line: Now go and check your last Reel.

short.title: Mini-story with a lesson
short.bestFor: Something that happened to you, told fast, ending on one thing the viewer can use.
short.footage: One take telling the story, plus photos, screenshots or clips of the moments you mention.
short.example: Worked example: the week our editor quit.
short.rhythm: A change every 2–4 seconds, slower on the emotional lines so they can land.
checks: Does the first line start after the boring part of the story?
Is there a moment of doubt before things turn?
Can you say the lesson in one sentence?

beats.title: Drop into the moment
beats.goal: Start at the worst or strangest moment and skip the setup.
beats.show: Tight on your face, no smile, the stakes on screen.
beats.line: Three days before launch, our only editor quit.

beats.title: Just enough context
beats.goal: Two sentences of who, what and why it mattered. Nothing more.
beats.show: Cut to a photo or clip of the situation while you keep talking.
beats.line: We had forty videos to deliver, a client waiting, and nobody else who could edit.

beats.title: What you tried
beats.goal: Show the first attempt and why it didn't work. The struggle keeps them watching.
beats.show: A receipt on screen with your face in a corner.
beats.line: So I tried to do it all myself, and two days later I'd finished four.

beats.title: The turn
beats.goal: Mark the moment things changed with a visual reset.
beats.show: A quick zoom, a new text line, one sound.
beats.line: Then a friend asked me one question that changed the plan.

beats.title: What changed
beats.goal: Say what you did differently, in concrete terms.
beats.show: The key number slammed on screen.
beats.line: She asked how many of the forty actually needed me. The honest answer was six.

beats.title: How it ended
beats.goal: Show the outcome with proof, not just a claim.
beats.show: Freeze on the result with a label.
beats.line: We delivered all of it on time, and I only edited the six that mattered.

beats.title: The lesson
beats.goal: One sentence they can use. Say it, then stop.
beats.show: Your face, punching in on the key word.
beats.line: You don't need more hours. You need to know which work actually needs you.

beats.title: End
beats.goal: Stop on the lesson, or ask one question for the comments.
beats.show: Hold a beat, then cut.
beats.line: Which part of your week is that?

short.title: Quick how-to
short.bestFor: Teaching one task in a few steps, on a screen or with your hands.
short.footage: The finished result, a screen recording or close-ups of each step, and you on camera for the opening.
short.example: Worked example: a two-minute colour grade on phone footage.
short.rhythm: A change every 2–3 seconds. Zoom on every control you touch and speed up any waiting.
checks: Can someone follow every step with the sound off?
Is every button and setting readable at phone size?
Is the before and after the same clip, at the same size and speed?

beats.title: Show the result
beats.goal: Open on the finished result, then say how long it takes.
beats.show: The result full screen, with the time it took on screen.
beats.line: This is a two-minute colour grade on phone footage.

beats.title: What they'll learn
beats.goal: Promise the exact steps, with a number.
beats.show: Your face, with a step counter appearing.
beats.line: Three sliders, in this order.

beats.title: Step 1
beats.goal: One action per step. Name it, do it, show the change.
beats.show: The screen recording, zoomed on the control.
beats.line: First, pull the highlights down until the sky has colour again.

beats.title: Step 2
beats.goal: Same pattern: name it, do it, show it.
beats.show: Back to your face for a beat, then the control.
beats.line: Then lift the shadows just enough to see the face clearly.

beats.title: Step 3
beats.goal: Finish the steps on the change that matters most.
beats.show: Zoom into the setting on the phone.
beats.line: Last, warm it up a touch. Most phone footage comes out too blue.

beats.title: Before and after
beats.goal: Show the full before and after at the same size.
beats.show: Split screen of the same clip.
beats.line: Raw on top, graded underneath. It's the same clip.

beats.title: End
beats.goal: Tell them what to do with it next: try it, save it, or the one mistake to avoid.
beats.show: Your face, with one line of text.
beats.line: Save this and try it on the next clip you film.

render.text: Save it for your next edit

short.title: List of three
short.bestFor: Three tips, tools or mistakes, with the best one saved for last.
short.footage: You on camera, plus a shot, screen or screenshot for each item.
short.example: Worked example: three cuts that save a boring take.
short.rhythm: A change every 2–3 seconds, with a counter that updates on every item.
checks: Does every item start with its number and its name?
Is the best item last, with a re-hook just before it?
Would the list still make sense with the sound off?

beats.title: Promise the number
beats.goal: Say the number and tease the best item.
beats.show: Your face with the promise on screen.
beats.line: Three cuts that save a boring talking-head take. The last one takes two seconds.

beats.title: Item 1
beats.goal: Name it in the first three words, then show it.
beats.show: A counter in the corner and the item on screen.
beats.line: One. Delete your first sentence. It's almost always a warm-up.

beats.title: Item 2
beats.goal: Keep the same pattern so viewers know where they are.
beats.show: Jump cuts on your face, counter updated.
beats.line: Two. Cut every pause longer than a breath, but keep your sentences whole.

beats.title: Re-hook before the best one
beats.goal: Tell them the last item is the one worth waiting for.
beats.show: A quick zoom and a new line of text.
beats.line: And the last one is the one nobody bothers with.

beats.title: Item 3, the best
beats.goal: Deliver the best item with the most visual energy.
beats.show: Punch in hard on the key word.
beats.line: Three. Punch in on the one word that matters in each sentence. That's the two-second fix.

beats.title: Recap
beats.goal: Run through all three in one breath, with the list on screen.
beats.show: The checklist full screen, your face in a corner.
beats.line: First sentence, pauses, punch-ins. Do all three on your next take.

beats.title: End
beats.goal: Ask which one they'll try, or loop back to the hook.
beats.show: Your face. Cut on the last word.
beats.line: Which one are you skipping?

short.title: Product or UGC demo
short.bestFor: Showing a product solving one real problem, without sounding like an ad.
short.footage: The product in use, the problem it solves, close-ups of two or three details, and the result.
short.example: Worked example: a phone grip that fixes shaky shots.
short.rhythm: Fast: a change every 1.5–2.5 seconds, with a sound on every contact and detail.
checks: Is the product in the first frame?
Is every claim shown on screen, not just said?
Is the ask a single line, with no fake urgency?

beats.title: Show it working
beats.goal: Open on the product mid-use, with the one claim on screen.
beats.show: The product in hand, with a short claim.
beats.line: This is a fifteen-dollar phone grip, and it fixed my shaky shots.

beats.title: The problem
beats.goal: Show the problem in one shot, ideally one the viewer has had too.
beats.show: The shaky footage, frozen on its worst frame.
beats.line: Every handheld walk I filmed looked like this.

beats.title: The details
beats.goal: Two or three details up close, one per cut, each with a word on screen.
beats.show: Zoom into each detail as you name it.
beats.line: It clips on in a second, the grip is rubber, and it folds flat in a pocket.

beats.title: In real use
beats.goal: Show it working somewhere real, not in a studio.
beats.show: The same walk, filmed with it on.
beats.line: Here's the same walk, filmed with it on.

beats.title: Before and after
beats.goal: Put the without and with side by side.
beats.show: Split screen, labeled.
beats.line: Without it on top. With it underneath.

beats.title: Soft ask
beats.goal: Say who it's for, in one line. No hard sell.
beats.show: One slammed line.
beats.line: If your shots shake, it's the cheapest fix I've found.

short.title: Podcast or interview clip
short.bestFor: Turning the best minute of a conversation into a clip that works on its own.
short.footage: A two-camera or two-shot recording, and the best 30–60 seconds of one answer.
short.example: Worked example: raising prices and losing the best clients.
short.rhythm: Cut on the speaker's rhythm, about every 3–4 seconds, and to the listener when a line lands.
checks: Does the clip make sense to someone who never heard the episode?
Does it start on the most surprising sentence, not the question?
Does it end on a strong line instead of trailing off?

beats.title: Start on the best line
beats.goal: Open on the most surprising sentence of the answer, even mid-thought.
beats.show: The speaker, with the stakes on screen.
beats.line: I raised my prices and lost my best clients.

beats.title: The question
beats.goal: Put the host's question on screen so the clip stands alone.
beats.show: The host reacting, with the question as text.
beats.line: Wait, you lost them? How does that even happen?

beats.title: The answer
beats.goal: Let the answer run, with cuts on pauses and punch-ins on emphasis.
beats.show: The speaker, jump cuts on the pauses.
beats.line: Because the ones paying the most wanted the work. They were never shopping for the cheapest option.

beats.title: The reaction
beats.goal: Cut to the listener when the line lands.
beats.show: The other person's face.
beats.line: Okay, that actually makes a lot of sense.

beats.title: Second turn
beats.goal: Open the next question before the energy drops.
beats.show: A quick zoom with a new line of text.
beats.line: But here's what I'd do differently next time.

beats.title: The takeaway
beats.goal: The practical bit, said plainly.
beats.show: The speaker, punching in on the key word.
beats.line: Raise prices for new clients first, and leave your best ones alone for a year.

beats.title: End on the strongest line
beats.goal: End on the strongest sentence, then cut. Name the full episode in the caption, not on screen.
beats.show: One slammed line.
beats.line: That one change kept every one of them.

short.title: React to a receipt
short.bestFor: Answering a comment, post or chart with your own evidence.
short.footage: You on camera and the screenshot, comment or chart, with private details blurred.
short.example: Worked example: a comment saying my edits are too fast.
short.rhythm: A change every 2–3 seconds. Put every receipt on screen while you talk about it.
checks: Is every receipt readable on a phone?
Are private names, emails and numbers blurred?
Do you say where you stand before you show the evidence?

beats.title: Show the receipt
beats.goal: Put the comment or post on screen in the first second and read the key words.
beats.show: The receipt full screen, your face in a corner circle.
beats.line: Someone said my edits are way too fast to follow. Let's check.

render.note: way too fast to follow tbh

beats.title: Your take, fast
beats.goal: Say where you stand in one sentence before the evidence.
beats.show: Your face, punching in on the turn in the sentence.
beats.line: Honestly, I thought they might be right.

beats.title: The evidence
beats.goal: Put the data on screen and point at the exact line.
beats.show: The chart full screen with the key part highlighted.
beats.line: So I pulled the numbers on my fastest and my slowest edits.

beats.title: The twist
beats.goal: Show the part that surprised you.
beats.show: A quick zoom and a new line of text.
beats.line: The fast one held people longer, but only for the first ten seconds.

beats.title: What it means
beats.goal: Turn the evidence into something the viewer can use.
beats.show: Split screen of the two edits.
beats.line: So the start needs to be fast, and the middle needs room to breathe.

beats.title: Answer the comment
beats.goal: Close the loop with the person who commented.
beats.show: Your face, with one line of text.
beats.line: So you were half right. Thanks for the comment.

short.title: Before and after
short.bestFor: A visible change: a build, a fix, a makeover, a clean-up.
short.footage: The before and after from the same angle, and three to five quick shots of the process.
short.example: Worked example: an old fence board turned into a shelf.
short.rhythm: Very fast in the middle: process shots under 2 seconds each, then a long hold on the reveal.
checks: Are the before and after shot from the same angle?
Is every process shot under two seconds?
Does the last frame cut cleanly back into the first?

beats.title: The before
beats.goal: Show the starting state and say what it is in a few words.
beats.show: The before shot, frozen for a beat, with a label.
beats.line: This board came off an old fence.

beats.title: The process, fast
beats.goal: Three to five quick shots of the work, each under two seconds, with a sound on every contact.
beats.show: Quick cuts of the work.
beats.line: Sand it, square the edges, then two coats of oil.

beats.title: The reveal
beats.goal: Hard cut to the after, from the same angle. Hold it.
beats.show: Before and after, side by side.
beats.line: And now it's the shelf in my kitchen.

beats.title: Loop
beats.goal: End on a line that cuts straight back into the first frame.
beats.show: One slammed line, then back to the start.
beats.line: One afternoon. Same board.

long.title: Talking-head explainer
long.bestFor: Teaching one idea or system in depth, mostly to camera.
long.footage: One long take of you, B-roll or screenshots for each claim, and the finished result.
long.example: Worked example: a one-page weekly plan.
long.rhythm: A visible change every 4–8 seconds. B-roll, screens or graphics for about a quarter of the runtime.
checks: Is the promise in the first 30 seconds, and specific?
Does every chapter start with a question or a claim, not 'okay, so'?
Does the ending return to the opening result?

beats.title: Cold open
beats.goal: Show the result or the most surprising claim in the first 10 seconds.
beats.show: The result, then your face with the title on screen.
beats.line: This one page plans my whole week in ten minutes.

beats.title: Promise
beats.goal: Say exactly what they'll be able to do by the end, and who it's for.
beats.show: Your face, punching in on the promise.
beats.line: By the end of this video, you'll have built one too, from a blank page.

beats.title: Roadmap
beats.goal: Show the chapters on screen in one beat, in under 15 seconds.
beats.show: The chapter list full screen, your face in a corner.
beats.line: It has four sections, and we'll start with the one most people skip.

beats.title: Chapter 1
beats.goal: Start the chapter with a question or a claim, then teach one thing.
beats.show: A chapter card, then your face with cutaways on every example.
beats.line: Section one is the part nobody plans: the things you won't do this week.

beats.title: Chapter 2
beats.goal: Same shape: open with a claim, teach, show an example.
beats.show: Your face, screens and cutaways.
beats.line: Section two is where the real tasks go, three a day at most.

beats.title: Mid-video re-hook
beats.goal: Around the middle, open a new loop: a mistake, a twist or a 'but'.
beats.show: A visual reset and a new line on screen.
beats.line: But this is where I nearly gave up on the whole system.

beats.title: Chapter 3
beats.goal: Pay off the re-hook inside this chapter.
beats.show: Your face, a receipt or two.
beats.line: The fix was a single box for the one thing that has to happen.

beats.title: Chapter 4
beats.goal: The last section, kept tight.
beats.show: Your face and the page being filled in.
beats.line: Section four takes two minutes on a Sunday night.

beats.title: Payoff
beats.goal: Return to the opening result and show it again with what they now know.
beats.show: The finished page from the cold open.
beats.line: Here's my page from this week, filled in.

beats.title: End screen
beats.goal: Point at one specific next video, not 'check out my other videos'.
beats.show: Your face with one video card beside you.
beats.line: If planning isn't your problem but finishing is, watch this one next.

long.title: Tutorial walkthrough
long.bestFor: A full how-to people will follow along with, step by step.
long.footage: Screen recordings or overhead shots of every step, you on camera for the intro and the checks, and the result.
long.example: Worked example: editing a ten-minute video in one evening.
long.rhythm: A change every 4–6 seconds. Zoom on every control and cut every wait.
checks: Could someone follow it with the video beside their own screen?
Is every control readable, with a zoom on each click?
Is there a check at the end so viewers know they did it right?

beats.title: Show the result
beats.goal: Open on the finished result and how long it took.
beats.show: The result playing, with the time on screen.
beats.line: This is a ten-minute video I edited in one evening.

beats.title: Promise and who it's for
beats.goal: Say what they'll make and what they need to start.
beats.show: Your face with the steps counter.
beats.line: You'll have the exact order I do it in, and you only need a free editor.

beats.title: Setup
beats.goal: Everything they need ready before step one, in under a minute.
beats.show: The screen, zoomed on the settings.
beats.line: Before we start, set your project to the same frame rate as your footage.

beats.title: Steps 1–2
beats.goal: One chapter per step. Name it, do it, show the result.
beats.show: A chapter card, then the screen with zooms.
beats.line: Step one: cut the whole thing down before you touch anything else.

beats.title: The common mistake
beats.goal: Show the mistake most people make here, before they make it.
beats.show: The wrong version, frozen with a label.
beats.line: This is the point where most people start adding music. Don't, yet.

beats.title: Steps 3–5
beats.goal: Same shape for each step. Speed up anything slow.
beats.show: Screen, zooms, counter.
beats.line: Step three is captions, and this is the setting that saves an hour.

beats.title: Check the result
beats.goal: Show how they can check they did it right.
beats.show: The finished export, played full screen.
beats.line: Play it back at full speed and check these three things.

beats.title: End screen
beats.goal: One next video that continues the skill.
beats.show: Your face with one video card.
beats.line: Next, here's how to make the first three seconds actually work.

long.title: Story or documentary
long.bestFor: Something that happened, told with tension, ending on what it means.
long.footage: Your narration or interview, footage or photos of each moment, and the place where it happened if you can film it.
long.example: Worked example: building a shelf that nearly didn't hold.
long.rhythm: A change every 5–8 seconds, slower on the emotional beats. Use the place and the objects to carry scenes.
checks: Does the cold open make sense with no context?
Is there a real setback before the midpoint?
Does the climax return to the cold-open moment?

beats.title: Cold open on the peak
beats.goal: Open on the most intense moment from later in the story, then cut away before it resolves.
beats.show: The peak moment, frozen just before the outcome.
beats.line: 'It's not going to hold.' Okay. Three weeks earlier, this was a pile of boards.

beats.title: What's at stake
beats.goal: Say what you were trying to do and why it mattered.
beats.show: The project and the deadline on screen.
beats.line: I had one weekend to build a bookshelf strong enough for all of these.

beats.title: The world before
beats.goal: Set up where you started, briefly, with the details that will matter later.
beats.show: Footage of the starting point.
beats.line: I'd built small things before, but never anything that had to carry weight.

beats.title: First attempt
beats.goal: What you tried, what went wrong, and what it cost.
beats.show: The process, with a freeze on the mistake.
beats.line: The first frame looked perfect until I leaned on it.

beats.title: Midpoint twist
beats.goal: Something changes the direction of the story.
beats.show: A visual reset and a new line.
beats.line: That's when I found out the problem wasn't the wood at all.

beats.title: Second attempt
beats.goal: The new approach, step by step, with rising tension.
beats.show: Process shots and close-ups.
beats.line: This time I built the joints first and the shelf around them.

beats.title: Climax
beats.goal: Return to the cold-open moment and finally show the outcome.
beats.show: The same shot as the cold open, played through.
beats.line: So, back to that moment. Last book, full weight.

beats.title: What it means
beats.goal: The lesson or the change in you, said simply.
beats.show: Your face, quieter.
beats.line: It held. And I learned to test the hardest part first.

beats.title: End screen
beats.goal: One next video that continues the story.
beats.show: One video card.
beats.line: The next build is the one that actually broke. It's here.

long.title: List or mistakes video
long.bestFor: Five to ten tips, tools or mistakes, counted down to the most important one.
long.footage: You on camera, plus an example, screen or demo for every item.
long.example: Worked example: five editing mistakes in beginners' first videos.
long.rhythm: A change every 4–6 seconds, and a chapter card with a counter on every item.
checks: Does the hook tease the most important item without giving it away?
Does every item have an example on screen?
Is there a re-hook before the last item?

beats.title: Tease the worst one
beats.goal: Say the number and tease the item you still struggle with.
beats.show: Your face with a counter.
beats.line: These are the five editing mistakes I see in almost every first video. Number four, I still make.

beats.title: Why it matters
beats.goal: Say what fixing these will change for them.
beats.show: A receipt that shows the cost.
beats.line: Each one quietly costs you viewers in the first ten seconds.

beats.title: Mistake 5
beats.goal: Name it, show an example, show the fix.
beats.show: A chapter card, then the example and the fix side by side.
beats.line: Number five: starting with 'hey guys, welcome back'.

beats.title: Mistakes 4–2
beats.goal: Same pattern for each one, with the counter updated.
beats.show: Chapter cards, examples and fixes.
beats.line: Number four is the one I still catch myself doing: music that's too loud.

beats.title: Before the last one
beats.goal: Tell them the last mistake is the one that matters most.
beats.show: A visual reset.
beats.line: The last one is the reason most of these videos never get finished.

beats.title: Mistake 1
beats.goal: The most important item, with the strongest example.
beats.show: Your face, a slam, the fix in action.
beats.line: Number one: trying to make the first video perfect.

beats.title: Recap
beats.goal: All five on screen as a checklist.
beats.show: The checklist full screen.
beats.line: Here are all five. Check your last video against them.

beats.title: End screen
beats.goal: One next video.
beats.show: One video card.
beats.line: If you fixed all five, this one's next.

long.title: Test or comparison
long.bestFor: Testing several options under the same rules and naming a winner.
long.footage: Every option filmed the same way, the test itself, and the results.
long.example: Worked example: five AI editing tools on the same raw clip.
long.rhythm: A change every 4–6 seconds. Split screens for every head-to-head, with scores on screen.
checks: Did every option get the same conditions?
Are the scores on screen, not just said?
Is the verdict clear, with who each option suits?

beats.title: The surprising result
beats.goal: Open on the most surprising result without naming the winner.
beats.show: Two results side by side.
beats.line: I tested five AI editing tools on the same raw clip. One of them cut my best line.

beats.title: The rules
beats.goal: Explain the test and what counts as a win.
beats.show: The rules as a checklist.
beats.line: Same clip, same prompt, and I score each one on three things.

beats.title: The contenders
beats.goal: Introduce each option in one line.
beats.show: Each option on screen with a counter.
beats.line: Five tools, two free and three paid. Let's start with the cheapest.

beats.title: Rounds
beats.goal: One round per option or per criterion, scores on screen after each.
beats.show: Split screens and score cards.
beats.line: Tool one got the pacing right but missed every punch-in.

beats.title: The twist
beats.goal: The result that changes the ranking.
beats.show: A visual reset.
beats.line: Then I watched them all with the sound off, and the ranking flipped.

beats.title: Verdict
beats.goal: Name the winner and why, then who should pick each of the others.

long.title: Podcast episode
long.bestFor: A full conversation that people stay with, with clips you can cut later.
long.footage: A two-camera or three-camera recording, with each person on their own microphone.
long.example: Worked example: an interview about pricing your work.
long.rhythm: Cut on intention, about every 5–10 seconds. Mark 3–5 moments in the edit that will work as Shorts.
checks: Is the cold open the best 20–30 seconds of the whole episode?
Do chapters have titles viewers can search for?
Have you marked the 3–5 moments that will become clips?

beats.title: Cold open
beats.goal: The best 20–30 seconds of the whole episode, before any intro.
beats.show: The guest at their sharpest, with the line on screen.
beats.line: We were forty minutes in when she said the thing that made us scrap the plan.

beats.title: Who and why now
beats.goal: Who the guest is and why this conversation matters now, in under a minute.
beats.show: Both people, with a lower third.
beats.line: She's priced over two hundred creative projects, and she thinks most of us are doing it backwards.

beats.title: Chapter 1
beats.goal: Open each chapter with a question that works as a title.
beats.show: A chapter card, then the conversation.
beats.line: So let's start with the first price you ever charged.

beats.title: Chapter 2
beats.goal: Keep the strongest exchanges, cut the warm-ups.
beats.show: The conversation, with reactions.
beats.line: When did you first lose a client over price?

beats.title: Mid-episode tease
beats.goal: Tease the moment from the cold open so people stay for it.
beats.show: A visual reset and a line on screen.
beats.line: And in a few minutes, she explains the one rule that changed everything.

beats.title: Chapter 3
beats.goal: The cold-open moment, in full context.
beats.show: The conversation.
beats.line: Here's the rule: price the outcome, not the hours.

beats.title: Last question
beats.goal: A short final question that gives the episode an ending.
beats.show: Both people.
beats.line: What would you tell yourself on your first project?

beats.title: Outro
beats.goal: One next episode, by name.
beats.show: One episode card.
beats.line: If this helped, the episode on contracts is the natural next one.
